reason: The picture shows the turning sensor cells at the base of a fluid-filled loop, where movement bends their hairs.
expectation: This should build the sensors that detect changes in head turning.

effect: The loops and cells form turning sensors: fluid movement bends the flap and changes a nerve signal. Next I can build the separate tilt sensors.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between fluid movement and the signal clearer.
reason: The mineral weights are shown resting on the jelly layer above the tilt sensor cells.
expectation: The weights and cells should form sensors that respond to tilt.

effect: The weighted layer shifts and bends hairs during tilt or changes in straight-line movement. Both kinds of sensor are now built.
reaction: The picture makes the weights' role clearer.
reason: Balance nerves are shown connecting both kinds of sensor to the brain, so I’ll connect the turning sensors first.
expectation: The turning sensors should gain a nerve route to the brain.

alternatives.reason: The tilt sensors also need a route to the brain.

effect: The turning sensors now have nerve fibres pointing toward the brain; the weighted sensors still need connecting.
reaction: The picture makes the incoming route clear.
reason: The balance nerves were consumed, so I’ll check how the weighted sensors can connect next.
expectation: The compatibility list should show how to connect the weighted sensors to the rest of the balance system.

effect: The inspection automatically joined both kinds of sensor to incoming nerve fibres leading toward the brain.
reaction: I was unsure how the weighted sensors would connect after the nerves were consumed, so the compatibility hint helped.
reason: The balance organs need to connect to the existing brain before their signals can help control eyes and posture.
expectation: The balance sensors should connect to the body's brain.

effect: The attempted body connection instead automatically linked the sensors through the brain to the eye and posture nerve routes. The muscle endpoints still need connecting.
reaction: The compatibility hint clarified the missing connection.
reason: The response connections have outlined body-muscle endpoints, so the existing body looks like the next fit.
expectation: The body should gain the connections needed to respond to head movement.

effect: The completed body shows how balance signals help keep the eyes on a fixed point and adjust posture, alongside vision and signals from muscles and joints.
reaction: Seeing the separate sensor routes come together in a visible response was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the weighted sensors was worthwhile because the picture showed how the weighted layer shifts and bends the sensing hairs during tilt or changes in straight-line movement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the weighted sensors was initially confusing because the balance nerves had been consumed. The inspection resolved it, but the required pairing was not obvious to me.

surprise.text: I expected to connect the sensors to the body first, but the game instead connected the eye and posture nerve routes through the brain.

arbitrary.text: The required order of connecting the response routes before fitting the body was not clear to me until the compatibility hint appeared, though the resulting picture explained the route.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter: building the sensors and seeing them produce a recognizable eye movement made me curious about other body connections, despite the unclear connection order.
